items.stem: What is meant by "Assignment of duties"?
items.answer: Allocating jobs to members of the organisation according to their skills and competencies.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Allocating jobs to members of the organisation according to their skills and competencies.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about organising is correct?
items.answer: Organising follows planning.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Organising follows planning.
options: Assignment of duties comes before division of work.
Organising leads to duplication of work.
Organising is the first function of management.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Departmentalisation is the first step of organising.
Reason (R): Departments are formed by grouping similar jobs.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: identification and division of work is the first step. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Delegation at Iyer Agencies gives junior managers a chance to take decisions and grow. Which point of importance of organising is highlighted?
items.answer: Development of personnel
items.markingKey: (a) Development of personnel. Delegation develops people.

items.stem: At Das Stores, it is made clear that the sales executives report to the sales manager. Which step of organising is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Establishing reporting relationships. Who reports to whom is fixed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Establishing reporting relationships; 2 marks for the justification: Who reports to whom is fixed.

items.stem:
Pooja started Jain Brothers to make electronic goods in Varanasi. As orders grew, she divided the work into jobs, grouped them into production, sales and finance departments, gave each job to suitable people and decided who would report to whom.
(i) Name the function and its steps followed by Pooja. (ii) State two benefits Jain Brothers will get.
items.answer: (i) Organising: identification and division of work; departmentalisation; assignment of duties; establishing reporting relationships. (ii) Specialisation; clarity in relationships; optimum use of resources; growth (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Organising: identification and division of work; departmentalisation; assignment of duties; establishing reporting relationships. (ii) Specialisation; clarity in relationships; optimum use of resources; growth (any two).

items.stem: At Goyal Enterprises, every employee knows whom to report to, so there is no confusion. Which point of importance of organising is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Clarity in working relationships. Relationships are clear.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Clarity in working relationships; 2 marks for the justification: Relationships are clear.

items.stem: Explain the following points of importance of organising: (i) Adaptation to change (ii) Clarity in working relationships.
items.answer: (i) Adaptation to change: The structure can be modified as needed. (ii) Clarity in working relationships: It is clear who reports to whom.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) The structure can be modified as needed. (ii) It is clear who reports to whom.

items.stem: Iyer Retail groups all purchase-related jobs into a purchase department. Which step of organising is described?
items.answer: Departmentalisation
items.markingKey: (c) Departmentalisation. Similar jobs are grouped.

items.stem: State any three advantages of a functional structure.
items.answer: Occupational specialisation; Coordination within a function; Managerial and operational efficiency; Minimal duplication of effort; Easy training of employees; Attention to all functional areas
items.markingKey: Any three of: Occupational specialisation; Coordination within a function; Managerial and operational efficiency; Minimal duplication of effort; Easy training of employees; Attention to all functional areas (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is true of functional structure but not of divisional structure?
items.answer: Specialisation: functional specialisation
items.markingKey: (d) functional structure: Specialisation: functional specialisation. The other options describe divisional structure.
options: Managerial development: easier, as divisional heads handle all functions
Responsibility: easy to fix for each division

items.stem:
Assertion (A): A divisional structure may increase costs.
Reason (R): Each division has its own functions, leading to duplication.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Joshi Enterprises, which sells mobile phones, laptops and televisions, plans to add a new division for cameras. Which organisation structure is suitable?
items.answer: Divisional structure
items.markingKey: (c) Divisional structure. New divisions can be added easily.

items.stem: Chopra Traders makes only kitchen appliances and needs a high degree of specialisation in production, finance and marketing. Which organisation structure is suitable? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Functional structure. A single-product firm with specialised functions.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Functional structure; 2 marks for the justification: A single-product firm with specialised functions.

items.stem: Which organisation structure is suitable? In each case give a reason. (i) Kapoor Brothers wants each product line to be a profit centre whose performance can be measured separately. (ii) Kapoor Brothers makes only mobile accessories and needs a high degree of specialisation in production, finance and marketing.
items.answer: (i) Divisional structure: Each division's performance can be measured. (ii) Functional structure: A single-product firm with specialised functions.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Divisional structure (ii) Functional structure

items.stem:
Reddy Traders began by making only spices with production, marketing and finance departments. It now also makes footwear and furniture, and the departments are struggling to coordinate the three products.
(i) Which structure does Reddy Traders have now, and which should it adopt? (ii) Give two reasons.
items.answer: (i) Functional structure; it should adopt a divisional structure. (ii) Product specialisation; accountability of each division; easier coordination; facilitates growth (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Functional structure; it should adopt a divisional structure. (ii) Product specialisation; accountability of each division; easier coordination; facilitates growth (any two).

items.stem:
Kulkarni Agencies began by making only medicines with production, marketing and finance departments. It now also makes footwear and furniture, and the departments are struggling to coordinate the three products.
(i) Which structure does Kulkarni Agencies have now, and which should it adopt? (ii) Give two reasons.
items.answer: (i) Functional structure; it should adopt a divisional structure. (ii) Product specialisation; accountability of each division; easier coordination; facilitates growth (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Functional structure; it should adopt a divisional structure. (ii) Product specialisation; accountability of each division; easier coordination; facilitates growth (any two).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about organisation structures is correct?
items.answer: A divisional structure makes it easy to fix responsibility.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: A divisional structure makes it easy to fix responsibility.
options: A divisional structure makes it easy to fix responsibility.
Span of management has no effect on the levels of management.
A functional structure suits firms with many unrelated products.
Functional empires arise in divisional structures only.

items.stem: Jain Stores wants to avoid duplication of effort and have experts head each function. Which organisation structure is suitable? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Functional structure. It minimises duplication and promotes specialisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Functional structure; 2 marks for the justification: It minimises duplication and promotes specialisation.

items.stem: Joshi Brothers wants each product line to be a profit centre whose performance can be measured separately. Which organisation structure is suitable?
items.answer: Divisional structure
items.markingKey: (a) Divisional structure. Each division's performance can be measured.

items.stem: Explain the following disadvantages of a functional structure: (i) Conflict of interests (ii) Emphasis on functional objectives.
items.answer: (i) Conflict of interests: Interests of departments may clash. (ii) Emphasis on functional objectives: Departmental goals may get more importance than organisational goals.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Interests of departments may clash. (ii) Departmental goals may get more importance than organisational goals.

items.stem: What is meant by "Formal organisation"?
items.answer: The organisation structure designed by management to accomplish a particular task, specifying relationships, authority and responsibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The organisation structure designed by management to accomplish a particular task, specifying relationships, authority and responsibility.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of formal organisation but not of informal organisation?
items.answer: Authority: arises by virtue of position
items.markingKey: (d) formal organisation: Authority: arises by virtue of position. The other options describe informal organisation.
options: Authority: arises out of personal qualities
Authority: arises by virtue of position

items.stem: Workers at Goyal and Sons who lunch together resisted a new shift system as a group. Is this an example of formal or informal organisation?
items.answer: Informal organisation
items.markingKey: (c) Informal organisation. Informal groups may resist change.

items.stem: The roles and duties of each manager at Kapoor Brothers are written in a manual. Is this an example of formal or informal organisation? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Formal organisation. Rules and procedures define roles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Formal organisation; 2 marks for the justification: Rules and procedures define roles.

items.stem:
Staff of Kulkarni Stores who travel together by bus learnt about a new incentive scheme before the official notice and helped explain it to others. Later, the same group spread a false rumour about lay-offs.
(i) Identify the type of organisation. (ii) State one advantage and one disadvantage shown.
items.answer: (i) Informal organisation (grapevine). (ii) Advantage: fast spread of communication; disadvantage: spreads rumours.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Informal organisation (grapevine). (ii) Advantage: fast spread of communication; disadvantage: spreads rumours.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the advantages of informal organisation?
items.answer: Fast spread of communication
items.markingKey: (c) "Fast spread of communication" is one of the advantages of informal organisation; the others are advantages of formal organisation.

items.stem: Explain the following advantages of formal organisation: (i) Easier to fix responsibility (ii) Stability.
items.answer: (i) Easier to fix responsibility: Mutual relationships are clearly defined. (ii) Stability: Behaviour of employees can be fairly predicted.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Mutual relationships are clearly defined. (ii) Behaviour of employees can be fairly predicted.

items.stem: State any three points of importance of decentralisation.
items.answer: Develops initiative among subordinates; Develops managerial talent for the future; Quick decision-making; Relief to top management; Facilitates growth; Better control
items.markingKey: Any three of: Develops initiative among subordinates; Develops managerial talent for the future; Quick decision-making; Relief to top management; Facilitates growth; Better control (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the points of importance of decentralisation?
items.answer: Basis of management hierarchy
items.markingKey: (b) "Basis of management hierarchy" is one of the points of importance of delegation, not one of the points of importance of decentralisation.
options: Develops managerial talent for the future

items.stem: Distinguish between delegation and decentralisation on the basis of purpose, scope, nature and status.
items.answer: (i) Purpose: delegation: to lessen the burden of the manager; decentralisation: to increase the role of subordinates by giving them more autonomy. (ii) Scope: delegation: narrow, limited to a superior and subordinates; decentralisation: wide, extending to the lowest level. (iii) Nature: delegation: a compulsory act, as no one can do everything alone; decentralisation: an optional policy decision. (iv) Status: delegation: a process followed to share tasks; decentralisation: the result of a policy decision of top management.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Purpose: delegation: to lessen the burden of the manager; decentralisation: to increase the role of subordinates by giving them more autonomy. (ii) Scope: delegation: narrow, limited to a superior and subordinates; decentralisation: wide, extending to the lowest level. (iii) Nature: delegation: a compulsory act, as no one can do everything alone; decentralisation: an optional policy decision. (iv) Status: delegation: a process followed to share tasks; decentralisation: the result of a policy decision of top management.

items.stem: Sharma Brothers allows its branch managers in every city to take most operating decisions. Which element of delegation is highlighted?
items.answer: Decentralisation
items.markingKey: (c) Decentralisation. Systematic delegation to the lowest levels.

items.stem: Rao and Sons allows its branch managers in every city to take most operating decisions. Which element of delegation is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Decentralisation. Systematic delegation to the lowest levels.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Decentralisation; 2 marks for the justification: Systematic delegation to the lowest levels.

items.stem: Which element of delegation is highlighted? In each case give a reason. (i) Sethi Agencies allows its branch managers in every city to take most operating decisions. (ii) Although Harleen delegated the work, she still has to answer to the director for the result.
items.answer: (i) Decentralisation: Systematic delegation to the lowest levels. (ii) Accountability: Accountability cannot be delegated.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Decentralisation (ii) Accountability

items.stem:
Farhan, the production head of Thakur Stores, asked Siddharth to complete an order of 5,000 units of garments and gave Siddharth the right to use overtime. The order was delayed and the director held Farhan answerable.
(i) Identify the three elements of delegation in the case. (ii) Was the director right to hold Farhan answerable? Why?
items.answer: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Siddharth to complete the order); accountability (Farhan answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Siddharth to complete the order); accountability (Farhan answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.

items.stem:
Lakshmi, the production head of Saxena Agencies, asked Manish to complete an order of 5,000 units of electronic goods and gave Manish the right to use overtime. The order was delayed and the director held Lakshmi answerable.

items.answer: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Manish to complete the order); accountability (Lakshmi answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Manish to complete the order); accountability (Lakshmi answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.

items.stem: Explain the following points of importance of delegation: (i) Motivation of employees (ii) Employee development.
items.answer: (i) Motivation of employees: Delegation shows trust and builds confidence. (ii) Employee development: Subordinates get a chance to use their talent.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Delegation shows trust and builds confidence. (ii) Subordinates get a chance to use their talent.

items.stem: What is meant by "Centralisation"?
items.answer: Concentration of decision-making authority at the top of the organisation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Concentration of decision-making authority at the top of the organisation.

items.stem:
Pillai Stores has grown to 40 stores across India. All decisions, even small ones, are still taken by the owner Saanvi, and store managers wait days for approval.
(i) What should Saanvi adopt? (ii) Give three benefits it will bring. (iii) Distinguish it from delegation on one basis.
items.answer: (i) Decentralisation. (ii) Quick decisions; relief to top management; initiative among subordinates; development of future managers; better control; facilitates growth (any three). (iii) Delegation is compulsory and narrow; decentralisation is an optional policy and wide in scope.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Decentralisation. (ii) Quick decisions; relief to top management; initiative among subordinates; development of future managers; better control; facilitates growth (any three). (iii) Delegation is compulsory and narrow; decentralisation is an optional policy and wide in scope.

items.markingKey: (c) "Employee development" is one of the points of importance of delegation; the others are points of importance of decentralisation.
options: Develops managerial talent for the future

items.stem: When online sales grew, Malhotra and Sons easily added a new e-commerce department. Which point of importance of organising is highlighted?
items.answer: Adaptation to change
items.markingKey: (c) Adaptation to change. The structure is flexible.

items.stem: Explain the following disadvantages of formal organisation: (i) Delay in action (ii) Lacks creativity.
items.answer: (i) Delay in action: Procedures must be followed. (ii) Lacks creativity: Rigid rules discourage new ideas.

items.stem: Distinguish between functional structure and divisional structure on the basis of cost, coordination, formation and managerial development.
items.answer: (i) Cost: functional structure: economical, with no duplication; divisional structure: costly, due to duplication of resources. Assertion (A): Decentralisation leads to quick decision making.
Reason (R): Decisions are taken by people close to the action.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both true; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Lakshmi gives the job of handling exports to an employee who knows foreign languages. Which step of organising is described?
items.answer: Assignment of duties
items.markingKey: (d) Assignment of duties. Jobs are matched to skills.

items.stem: Distinguish between functional structure and divisional structure on the basis of cost, specialisation, formation and responsibility.
items.answer: (i) Cost: functional structure: economical, with no duplication; divisional structure: costly, due to duplication of resources. (ii) Specialisation: functional structure: functional specialisation; divisional structure: product specialisation. (iii) Formation: functional structure: based on functions; divisional structure: based on product lines, supported by functions. (iv) Responsibility: functional structure: difficult to fix on a department; divisional structure: easy to fix for each division.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Cost: functional structure: economical, with no duplication; divisional structure: costly, due to duplication of resources. (ii) Specialisation: functional structure: functional specialisation; divisional structure: product specialisation. (iii) Formation: functional structure: based on functions; divisional structure: based on product lines, supported by functions. (iv) Responsibility: functional structure: difficult to fix on a department; divisional structure: easy to fix for each division.

items.stem: At Agarwal Industries, the sales executives report to the sales manager as laid down in the organisation chart. Is this an example of formal or informal organisation?
items.answer: Formal organisation
items.markingKey: (b) Formal organisation. Relationships are defined by management.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the points of importance of decentralisation?
items.answer: Better control
items.markingKey: (a) "Better control" is one of the points of importance of decentralisation; the others are points of importance of delegation.

items.stem:
Ishaan, the production head of Mehta Brothers, asked Kabir to complete an order of 5,000 units of bicycles and gave Kabir the right to use overtime. The order was delayed and the director held Ishaan answerable.
(i) Identify the three elements of delegation in the case. (ii) Was the director right to hold Ishaan answerable? Why?
items.answer: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Kabir to complete the order); accountability (Ishaan answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Authority (right to use overtime); responsibility (Kabir to complete the order); accountability (Ishaan answerable). (ii) Yes, accountability cannot be delegated.

items.stem: State one difference between functional structure and divisional structure on the basis of specialisation.
items.answer: functional structure: functional specialisation; divisional structure: product specialisation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: functional structure: functional specialisation; divisional structure: product specialisation
